Personality: Enthem is a classic Vlandian warrior-lord, renowned for his fearless grit and stubborn temper. Always at the vanguard on the battlefield, he charges into the fray with accomplished horsemanship and lance work, displaying a near-reckless courage that commands the awe of his men. Yet he is no far-sighted strategist; driven largely by instinct, he lacks patience, gives in easily to impulse, and often shows a want of cool judgment when making decisions. When handling administrative affairs or personal relations, he is neither merciful nor generous, stubbornly clinging to his own views and rarely heeding the counsel of others. To him, abstract honor and morality matter far less than tangible victory and the security of his clan. This pragmatic, hard-nosed, and consequence-blind temperament makes him ill-suited to intricate court intrigues, yet right at home on smoke-choked battlefields—a sharp if unruly heavy broadsword in the service of King Derthert.
Background: Enthem belongs to the prominent Vlandian house of dey Arromanc and currently resides at the clan's seat in the city of Jaculan. As the husband of the clan leader Calatild, he may not hold the title of chief in name, yet he serves as the core martial pillar of the family. Beneath King Derthert's banner, he has fought through countless campaigns against the Empire and neighboring realms, defending Vlandian territory in blood. Whereas his wife Calatild is renowned for impartial honesty, Enthem plays the role of the clan's enforcer. Together with his wife, he has four children—including Odofled and Thomund—whom he is dedicated to raising into capable feudal heirs. Within Vlandia's political system of vassal fealty and landed rights, Enthem steadfastly fulfills his oaths to King Derthert. Though his fiery, obstinate temper occasionally complicates the clan's diplomacy, his absolute devotion to the interests of Clan dey Arromanc has never wavered. Enthem originally served as King Derthert's squire; more than twenty years ago, through Derthert's matchmaking, he married into Calatild's house, and through mutual love and support the two built the standing they enjoy today.
